key_insight: The paper argues that LoRA adapters should be treated as information carriers that can be safely read from, but not arbitrarily rewritten into one another. By identifying the hidden degrees of freedom in LoRA factorization, the authors show why naive adapter merging causes interference and how to compose skills more reliably.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of combining multiple independently trained LoRA adapters into a single model without losing task performance, requiring expensive retraining, or falling back to routing across separate adapters.
method: Analyze why standard LoRA merging fails by exposing the two implicit choices made during composition: factorization gauge and write-back direction.
Design a composition strategy that preserves useful adapter information while avoiding destructive interference in weight space.
Use the insight that LoRA skills should be read for reuse, but not directly written back into a shared update matrix.
impact: This can make multi-task adapter reuse more practical and stable for large language models. For practitioners, it offers a cheaper path to combining specialized skills without retraining from scratch or maintaining many separate adapters.
visual_elements: Diagram of multiple LoRA adapters being merged into one model, showing interference in naive merging versus clean composition in the proposed method.

paper_title: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
paper_authors: Zeyan Li, Panqi Yang, Qirong Guo, Shengda Zhuo, SIyuan Qiu
